title: Are heavy metals linked to autism in kids?

grade.title: No qualifying human study in this corpus
grade.outcome: Metals as a cause of autism
grade.basis: No qualifying human study of that link was located in this corpus.

answerHtml: No study in this corpus tests a causal link between heavy metals and autism. The question is not graded. A separate question, whether DMSA improves autism symptoms, was reviewed by Cochrane: one flawed randomized trial, no evidence of benefit, and a statement that risks outweigh proven benefits. That grade is on the DMSA page.

sections.heading: The chelation trial is a different claim
sections.html: James and colleagues (2015) included the Adams trial and concluded there was no evidence of an effect on autism symptoms. doi:10.1002/14651858.CD010766.pub2. CDC also reported a death in a child with autism given disodium EDTA. MMWR 2006.

sources.text: James et al. 2015 Cochrane review, PMID 26114777

buyHtml:
The Heavy Metal Tested and Certified public register listed no licensees on 15 October 2026. That page reported 0 certified brands and 0 certified products, and it stated that no brand has completed the three-lot baseline. A specimen layout on the register is an illustration, not a licensee. This page does not name or rank any brand.

The program states that certification is a measurement of a product against a published limit, not a statement that the product is safe. If a licensee is later listed for this category, it will be on the register.
